definition: A commonly used method that modifies the Black-Scholes formula to approximate the value of a spread option.
core_idea: Because spread options cannot be exactly priced with standard option formulas, practitioners use approximation techniques like Kirk's approximation to adapt Black-Scholes for two-asset spread payoffs.
key_points: Named as one of the key topics of the chapter but the specific formula is not given in this excerpt.
Positioned as a practical workaround for the fact that spreads don't fit lognormal, single-asset option pricing assumptions.
relationships: Modification of the Black-Scholes formula for spread options.
